title: SLO surface mesh and priority preemption playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a concise, implementable playbook that defines the SLO/SLI surface across model endpoints and maps priority-aware preemption policies for multi-region failover and load shedding. This ticket synthesizes per-endpoint SLI definitions (latency/quality/availability), error-budget accounting rules, circuit breaker thresholds, and a deterministic preemption policy that the routing/arbiter layer can consume. The output should include: canonical SLI definitions by endpoint category; a schema for SLO declarations that teams can adopt; clear error-budget burn and escalation rules; concrete circuit-breaker trigger values and hysteresis; prioritized load-shedding order for model variants, routes, and tenants; and a staged rollout checklist with telemetry gates and automated mitigation actions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Canonical SLI definitions published for three endpoint categories: conversational-chat, short-completion (sync), and high-throughput-embed routes
A2: SLO declaration schema (YAML/JSON example) validated with Console team and added to runtime-1.22 release notes
A3: Error-budget accounting procedure documented: burn-rate thresholds, auto-throttle steps, and on-call escalation playbook
A4: Circuit breaker policy matrix with numeric thresholds (percent error, p95 latency, instance saturation) and backoff/hysteresis values
A5: Priority preemption policy that maps tenant/route/variant to preemption buckets and a deterministic algorithm for runtime arbitration
A6: Integration checklist for rollout including telemetry dashboards, smoke-tests, and a canary plan; signoff from Reliability and Console leads
notes: Scope limited to inference endpoints and routing layer; storage and control-plane long-lived operations are out of scope for this ticket
We prefer SLOs expressed as composite contracts (availability + request-quality) so teams can reason about trade-offs between latency and result quality
Decision: Use three priority buckets (P0 critical, P1 business-critical, P2 best-effort) for preemption. Final mapping will be configurable per-customer but defaults will be opinionated
Trade-off: Aggressive preemption reduces burst latency for critical workloads but increases perceived failure for preempted tenants; include transparent logs and a compensation page in Console
technical_spec_highlights:
SLI definitions (examples):
- availability: successful response rate (2xx or structured success) over 7d rolling window
- latency: p95 tail in ms measured at ingress after routing decision
- quality: promptset-based token-normalized embedding cosine/response-acceptance measured via eval hooks

SLO templates (examples):
- conversational-chat: availability 99.9% (7d), p95 latency < 350ms (1d), quality acceptance >= 98% (rolling 14d)
- short-completion: availability 99.95% (7d), p95 latency < 150ms (1d)
- embeddings/high-throughput: availability 99.99% (7d), median latency < 60ms
Error-budget policy: burn-rate bands -> passive alert at 2x burn; active mitigation start at 5x burn; immediate escalation and possible throttling at 10x burn

Circuit breaker triggers (defaults):
- error-rate > 2% sustained for 5m -> soft-breaker (reject 5% traffic)
- error-rate > 5% sustained for 2m -> hard-breaker (reject 30% traffic)
- p95 latency > SLO threshold * 1.5 for 10m -> engage latency shedding path
Hysteresis/backoff: exponential backoff windows with minimum 2m cooldown and doubling up to 32m; re-enable traffic at incremental steps tied to recovered SLI signals

Priority preemption algorithm: deterministic ranking by (priority bucket, SLO importance weight, token-cost-per-request, pinned-variant flag). Arbitration results are stable under equal inputs and documented in playbook
Telemetry: require synthetic canary traffic for each route, delta SLI monitors, and per-tenant burn counters visible in Console
runbook_steps: 1) Observe burn alarm: check per-route burn rate, top offending tenants and variants
2) If burn between 2x-5x: enable adaptive batching adjustments and increase prefix (KV) cache retention for affected routes
3) If burn between 5x-10x: apply preemption according to priority buckets (start with P2 > P1 > P0) and enable canary rollback for new model variants
4) If burn >10x or service impact high: initiate regional circuit breaker for affected region and route traffic to secondary region with higher capacity
5) Post-incident: run retrospective, allocate error-budget debt, and schedule mitigation tech debt tickets (e.g., model quantization, autoscale config)
examples_and_edge_cases: Edge: A high-volume non-critical embeddings tenant (P2) spikes and consumes KV cache leading to p95 latency regression for P0 chat routes in same region -> policy should preempt embeddings (drop to best-effort) and warm standby in second region

Edge: A new model variant causes quality regression but does not change latency -> SLOs tied to quality need pre-deployment gates; include quality SLI in canary and abort rollout on 3% drop in quality acceptance
Regional failover: prefer graceful drain + shift small percentage (10%) initially; if secondary region SLOs degrade, fall back to rate-limited operation and notify on-call
